messages:
Marta: FYI after the device-plugin v0.9.2 rollout in us-west1 we're observing a cluster-wide scheduling wobble. Lots of GPU pods land in ContainerCreating or ImagePullBackOff during the driver init step.

Devin: Can you paste the node-level kubelet logs or init-container stderr? sounds like kernel module or DKMS issues.

Marta: paste from a node: ```MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "nvidia-driver": failed to exec driver-installer: exit status 1
stderr: "dkms: ERROR: could not locate module source"```
Nodes report dkms rebuild failures and missing /proc/driver/nvidia.

Kai: did the plugin change advertising logic? I remember a change that advertises capacity earlier to reduce scheduling latency.

Samir: Correct — PR #412 moved advertise to happen sooner (reduce cold-start blips). That speeds capacity visibility but can advertise GPUs before DKMS completes.

Marta: Result: scheduler bound ~120 GPU pods across multiple nodes. Init containers tried to build drivers, failed, and then pods stalled. Kubelet churn increased and we hit node eviction thresholds.

infra-bot: [alert] 1999991111 - gpu-operator: driver-init-failures spike in us-west1 (10m trend)

Devin: Immediate: cordon the worst-performing hosts, drain GPU pods gracefully. Start rollback: device-plugin -> v0.9.1 in canary namespace.

Kai: Also add a simple readiness gate in the daemonset so the plugin does not advertise until driver present. Something like: ```#!/bin/sh
set -e
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  if [ -e /proc/driver/nvidia ] || command -v nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    exit 0
  fi
  sleep 1
done
exit 1
```
This prevents early advertise on slow-init nodes.

Samir: Good. I'll open a quick operator patch to hold advertise until a successful driver check. Also propose a preflight that verifies kernel-headers match and DKMS can compile for older pools.

Marta: I've started cordon/drain on 8 affected nodes in the older kernel pool. Rolling rollback in canary in 5m and monitoring. Opening ticket INFRA-7901 with logs and repro steps.

ops-bot: @channel rollback initiated: device-plugin v0.9.2 -> v0.9.1 (canary) | monitoring 5m checks

Devin: Longer term: schedule a kernel-header sync job for the legacy node pool and a DKMS package backfill. Also add scheduler affinity preference for nodes labelled gpu-ready=true to reduce re-scheduling during rollouts.

Kai: I'll own the header sync and add an e2e that simulates slow module probe so we catch regressions in CI.

Samir: Pushed a hotfix PR to gate advertise, linking the PR in INFRA-7901. Also adding a rate-limited re-advertise to avoid surfacing transient capacity.

Marta: Thanks all. Can everyone ping here once the canary is green or if we see re-ads after the rollback. :thumbsup:

Devin: I'll assemble a short incident note: root cause = advertise-before-driver-ready + DKMS/kernel-header drift on older nodes. Action items: (1) rollback plugin, (2) add readiness gate, (3) kernel-header backfill, (4) e2e for slow-probe.

Marta: Status update: canary returned healthy at +12m. Starting staggered rollback across remaining nodes with 10-node batches. Monitoring latency and pod success.

infra-bot: [info] 1999991450 - rollback progress: canary ok, batch 1 success

Kai: created e2e test case and local repro script to throttle udev/DKMS timeouts; will add to CI.

Samir: also adding scheduler cfgmap tweak: prefer nodes with label `gpu-ready=true` for 24h post-rollback to avoid immediate churn.

Marta: filing postmortem draft in INFRA board, will include logs, timeline, and the remediation checklist.

Devin: Great work. Once headers backfill completes, we should run a DKMS smoke job across the legacy pool.

Marta: assigning follow-ups and closing this thread after the postmortem. Thanks everyone.
